claims.text: POL-NS-01 is conjunctive, and limb (b) is simply not met on this record. The driver's trace carries 93 fixes across the whole window, yet derived.arrival.qualifying_fix_count is 0 and the longest qualifying run is 0 fixes lasting 0.0 seconds — not the three consecutive admissible in-radius fixes the clause requires. The 'arrived' event at 08:12:35 therefore starts nothing, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the cancellation fee is not chargeable under the anchor clause.

Run the POL-NS-02 arithmetic as the clause directs: the STANDARD arrival radius is 50 m and the test needs at least three consecutive fixes each reporting horizontal accuracy of 25 m or better. The driver's closest recorded approach is 37.94 m, which is inside the radius on its face — but no fix in the trace qualifies, because every in-radius reading failed the 25 m accuracy filter (that is precisely why qualifying_fix_count is 0). POL-NS-02 says fixes reporting worse than 25 m accuracy are ignored for this test and count as evidence of neither presence nor absence. The trace honestly reports poor horizontal accuracy in the Raffles Place urban canyon; that is what it measures, and the clause does not let it be read up into an arrival. There is no admissible arrival, so POL-NS-02 gives the rider a full refund of the cancellation fee.

The dispute is rider-filed (filed_by RIDER) and the fare ledger shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00 against a cancellation fee of 4.00. Under POL-GEN-03 a FULL_REFUND returns the whole contested amount to the filing party, and there is no compound outcome here to net against: no driver payment can arise on these facts (POL-NS-07 requires POL-NS-01 satisfied in full). The rider-side outcome is therefore the full 4.00, not a partial or a hold.

Independently of the arrival test, POL-NS-06 refunds the fee in full where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the 300 second minimum for STANDARD. The measured in-geofence dwell on this trace is zero: accumulated_dwell reports run_count 0 and a shortfall_sec of 300.0, built on the 300 second zone minimum and the 300 m leash. POL-NS-06 is explicit that the refund follows 'whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages', so even a driver who disputes rider presence has no answer to a 300 second shortfall.

The only mechanism that could bridge a zero dwell is POL-NS-06(i), which sums separate in-geofence intervals, and it requires a traffic_advisory that is present and populated and carries a type of KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT covering the pickup road for the waiting period. EV-ADVIS-00212-01 is MISSING: no payload, weight_multiplier 0.0, a BLOCKING MISSING_ARTIFACT issue, and the derived block records limb (i) as available: false for both want of a second interval and want of an advisory. I cite the absence, not the advisory: nothing in this bundle permits dwell to be accumulated, and nothing cures the 300 second shortfall.

POL-NS-03 offers the driver no escape from a refund. Its first sentence returns the cancellation fee to the rider in full wherever the driver held position outside the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin — the trace shows the driver's closest recorded approach at 37.94 m, well inside that ceiling — and its fault allocation then turns on the chat log. The rider's message reads 'im at exit A, which car ah? i dont see anything here' and the registered pickup point is labelled 'Raffles Place MRT (Exit A)', so under POL-NS-03(i) the rider named the correct entrance and the loss is the driver's. If, on the other hand, the 400 m branch is not reached at all, POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06 govern and the refund is still full. There is no branch of this policy on which the 4.00 stays charged to a rider who stood at the pin.

POL-NS-07 pays the driver 80 percent of the fee only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it. Limb (b) is not satisfied and POL-NS-06 displaces the fee, so the 3.20 of 4.00 driver_compensation figure in the fare derivation never becomes payable, and the 4.00 remains a rider refund rather than a payout. The anti-farming limb is also not tripped — no_show_terminations_30d of 2 against completed_trips_30d of 132, nowhere near the 4-or-more and above-0.08 test — so there is no route by which the fee is withheld and held against this rider.

I concede POL-NS-04 on the rider's side, and I do not need it. The chat log shows the rider's locating message sent at 08:15:02 and the driver replying at 08:15:30 — 28 seconds later, inside the 120 second window in limb (b) — which the admissibility note on the chat artifact records as taking the case out of POL-NS-04 whatever the reply said. This clause does not exonerate the rider; POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06 carry the refund instead.

No POL-NS-09 trigger fires, so the fee should be refunded rather than placed on hold. The artifact that decides the case, EV-GPS-00212, is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 with 100 percent coverage, zero gaps and a 10 second cadence, so confidence is not capped below the 0.70 floor under POL-GEN-02(2); no admissible artifact contradicts another on arrival, dwell or rider presence; the same-party counters are 0 and 0, so the repeat-dispute and abuse limbs are silent; and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip. This is a decidable case with a clean deciding artifact, and the disposition is a full refund of the cancellation fee.

The rider's own track corroborates rather than undercuts her account, and the record contains nothing that puts her elsewhere. Her device logs 60 fixes from 08:08:00 to 08:22:00, all stationary on a single distinct speed of 0.0, with a worst-case distance of 40.37 m and a mean of 22.57 m from the pickup pin — consistent with someone standing at the kerb she named 19 minutes earlier. I disclose that every one of those fixes fails the 25 m accuracy filter, so under POL-NS-02 they are neutral and I do not ask the Judge to treat them as proof of presence; the point is that the bundle supplies no admissible evidence of rider absence either, and POL-NS-06 makes presence irrelevant to the refund in any event.

claims.text: POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) are satisfied on this record and the rider cannot win by attacking either. Limb (a): the trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event for TRP-00212 at 08:12:35. Limb (d): the trip records no boarding event and shows the trip terminated by the driver at 08:20:30 with cancellation_reason_code EXCESSIVE_WAIT, which is one of the three codes limb (d) recognises — the admissibility pre-pass says so expressly. The way this driver closed the trip is therefore lawful under the anchor clause, and no adverse finding about the termination itself is available.

POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider and cannot be used to strip the fee of its foundation. Limb (a) is met — the rider's 08:15:02 message ('im at exit A, which car ah? i dont see anything here') is a locating message — but limb (b) plainly fails: the driver replied at 08:15:30, twenty-eight seconds later, far inside the 120 second window, and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty. The pre-pass reaches the same conclusion: the 28-second reply 'takes the case out of POL-NS-04 whatever the reply said'. Limb (b) is conjunctive with limb (a), so the clause does not apply, and any residual mislocation falls to be decided under POL-NS-03.

POL-NS-05 is not engaged, so the false-arrival finding and the POL-NS-05(ii) referral it carries are not in play against this driver. The clause needs a positive finding at the 'arrived' timestamp that the driver was more than 300 m from the pin or travelling at 15 km/h or above, and no derived fact in the trace supplies either — the arrival block reports no matching fix, and there is no timestamp-distance series to support the trigger. The only positional datum the derived driver track gives is a minimum distance of 37.94 m from the pickup pin, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and an order of magnitude inside the 300 m band.

The reason the trace yields zero qualifying in-geofence fixes is the device's reported horizontal accuracy, not the driver's absence. All 93 driver fixes and all 60 rider fixes fall outside the 25 m filter; the artifact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and, as its admissibility note says, honestly reports what the device measured. POL-NS-02 provides in terms that fixes reporting accuracy worse than 25 m 'count as evidence of neither presence nor absence'. On the driver's location this trace is therefore non-probative in both directions: it cannot affirmatively place him outside the geofence, and the shortfall the rider needs rests on the absence of qualifying fixes rather than on any evidence that he was elsewhere.

The rider's own device contradicts the picture of a driver who never came. Her track runs from 08:08:00 to 08:22:00 with 60 fixes, a single distinct speed of 0.0 km/h — she was standing still throughout — a mean distance of 22.57 m and a maximum of 40.37 m from the pickup pin. On the same pin, the driver's track records a closest reported approach of 37.94 m. On the trace's own reported figures both parties were at the pickup pin during the waiting window, which is consistent with the failed kerbside meet-up the driver describes and inconsistent with the rider's assertion that there was no vehicle at that kerb.

POL-NS-03 is not the route to a driver-side finding either. Its precondition is a trace showing the driver stationary for the required dwell at a point outside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius but not more than 400 m from the pin. This trace reports no stationary in-geofence interval at all — run_count 0, runs empty, longest_run_sec 0.0 — and its closest reported approach to the pin, 37.94 m, is inside the 50 m STANDARD radius. Whatever is disputed about the waiting period, the record does not show this driver holding position at the wrong face of the pickup point; the driver was not somewhere else.

There is no fare defect and no room for a partial refund on integrity grounds. The 4.00 charged is the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee (4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (4.00) — a tie under fee_schedule.resolution_rule, as the pre-pass itself notes — and the fare breakdown's derived money block reports a difference of 0.00, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged and the amount itemised needs no revisiting.

The anti-farming guard does not trip and no abuse escalation is open on either side. POL-NS-07's check reads exactly two fields: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2 against completed_trips_30d of 132 — 1.5 percent, below both the absolute threshold of 4 and the 0.08 rate — so nothing is withheld from this driver and no POL-NS-09(d) escalation follows from his side; rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, so the rider-side limb does not trip either. Under POL-GEN-01 only those named counters may be used for this test; the driver's prior_no_show_flags, rating and acceptance_rate are context only, and I do not ask the judge to find on any of them.

The driver's primary ask is that the charge stand. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION means the filing party's claim is not supported and the present state — payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00 — is left as it is. The rider's claim, that no silver Corolla ever came to the kerb, is supported by no artifact that affirmatively places this driver outside the geofence: the case against him is an inference drawn from fixes that the accuracy filter discarded, while her own trace shows her standing at the pin she was told the car was at. On that record her claim is not made out and the fee should stand.

In the alternative, if the judge cannot run the location test at all, the case should escalate under POL-NS-09(b) with the fee held rather than refunded. The decisive question — was the driver inside the geofence, and for how long — is carried by two admissible artifacts that point in opposite directions and that no clause resolves here: the trip record (weight 1.0) records an arrival event at 08:12:35 and a wait of 7.9 minutes, while the trace (weight 1.0) yields zero qualifying in-geofence fixes and zero dwell seconds. POL-NS-02's 25 m filter makes every fix non-probative in both directions, so neither document can be preferred, and POL-NS-06's shortfall arithmetic is run without one of the artifacts that clause requires. On that artifact: EV-ADVIS-00212-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, the pre-pass's only BLOCKING flag; I cite its absence and not any content, and I do not assert POL-NS-06(i), which its absence makes unavailable. The rider should not be paid out on evidence that cannot place this driver anywhere.

If the judge is satisfied on arrival and dwell, the driver's remedy is POL-NS-07 and it is money in cash, not a mere refusal to refund. Compensation is 80 percent of the cancellation fee itemised in the fare breakdown — computed there as 3.20 of 4.00 — the residual 20 percent being the platform service fee, and the anti-farming check does not withhold it. The ruling value on such a finding is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd mirroring driver_compensation_sgd per POL-GEN-03, and the disposition of the fee is NO_ACTION. I put this in the alternative so the judge has the driver's arithmetic whatever she finds on location.

ledger.claim: The driver's primary ask is that the charge stand. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION means the filing party's claim is not supported and the present state — payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00 — is left as it is. The rider's claim, that no silver Corolla ever came to the kerb, is supported by no artifact that affirmatively places this driver outside the geofence: the case against him is an inference drawn from fixes that the accuracy filter discarded, while her own trace shows her standing at the pin she was told the car was at. On that record her claim is not made out and the fee should stand.

In the alternative, if the judge cannot run the location test at all, the case should escalate under POL-NS-09(b) with the fee held rather than refunded. The decisive question — was the driver inside the geofence, and for how long — is carried by two admissible artifacts that point in opposite directions and that no clause resolves here: the trip record (weight 1.0) records an arrival event at 08:12:35 and a wait of 7.9 minutes, while the trace (weight 1.0) yields zero qualifying in-geofence fixes and zero dwell seconds. POL-NS-02's 25 m filter makes every fix non-probative in both directions, so neither document can be preferred, and POL-NS-06's shortfall arithmetic is run without one of the artifacts that clause requires. On that artifact: EV-ADVIS-00212-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, the pre-pass's only BLOCKING flag; I cite its absence and not any content, and I do not assert POL-NS-06(i), which its absence makes unavailable. The rider should not be paid out on evidence that cannot place this driver anywhere.

If the judge is satisfied on arrival and dwell, the driver's remedy is POL-NS-07 and it is money in cash, not a mere refusal to refund. Compensation is 80 percent of the cancellation fee itemised in the fare breakdown — computed there as 3.20 of 4.00 — the residual 20 percent being the platform service fee, and the anti-farming check does not withhold it. The ruling value on such a finding is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd mirroring driver_compensation_sgd per POL-GEN-03, and the disposition of the fee is NO_ACTION. I put this in the alternative so the judge has the driver's arithmetic whatever she finds on location.
